summary.verdict: HONEST TENSION (both naive and hard-filter are wrong in different ways). SAFETY: the corrected pipeline is safe by construction (0 host-toxic in top-k both orgs) whereas the NAIVE conservation shortlist would include {'mtb': 5, 'ecoli': 9} host-toxic (human-essential-homolog) targets — a real safety gain. TOP-K RECALL looks nearly preserved (corrected/naive {'mtb': 0.812, 'ecoli': 1.0}; precision@k mtb 0.2388->0.194, ecoli 0.2766->0.2766). BUT THE REAL COST IS LARGE AND STRUCTURAL: a blunt sequence-level host-non-homology hard filter PERMANENTLY EXCLUDES {'mtb': 0.522, 'ecoli': 0.351} of ALL known drug targets (those WITH a human homolog) from the searchable space — the pipeline can NEVER find them. Top-k recall only looks preserved because base recall is low and the surviving host-non-homologous targets rank well mechanistically. Many host-homologous targets ARE drugged SELECTIVELY in reality by exploiting binding-site differences a sequence filter cannot see. NET: naive-conservation is UNSAFE (promotes host-toxic); the hard filter is SAFE but OVER-EXCLUDES 52% of real targets; the genuinely correct selectivity needs BINDING-SITE-level pathogen-vs-host difference reasoning (structure, not sequence homology) — which sequence transfer cannot provide (another instance of the information ceiling). Abstention IS calibrated (no-homolog genes are target-poor). SCOPE: metabolic subproteome; 2 bacteria; unsupervised zero-label composite; ChEMBL selection-bias likely UNDER-estimates exclusion for a truly novel pathogen; molecule-half stage weak (C1/HIT2); not wet-lab.
